title: upgrade-attn-flashattnv2-rotary-fused-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Upgrade FlashAttentionV2 kernels and fuse rotary + ROPE ops for improved throughput and reduced memory pressure; introduce a new fused-kv-prefetch path and scheduler hints to enable continuous KV batching across short-lived chat sessions. Motivation: production P95 token latency and GPU utilization regressions observed on long-turn dialogues with existing attention kernels. This PR upgrades the attention kernels to the FlashAttentionV2 codepath with custom patches to support fused rotary/rope computation and a contiguous KV layout to reduce kernel launch overhead. It also adds scheduling hints on the runtime request path to prefer KV-prefetch-friendly batching for chat routes, and a small opt-in feature flag to toggle the fused path per model. Changeset summary: kernel patches (+CUDA C++), runtime scheduler updates (+Go), small Python test harness updates for microbenchmarks, and perf test artifacts. Benchmarks: +18% throughput on Llama-2-13B under typical chat workload, -12% mean GPU memory allocations, P95 token latency reduced by 9% on constrained batches. Includes compatibility fallbacks for models without rotary embeddings. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Can you share the microbenchmark harness and the exact workload used for the 18% throughput number? Need reproducibility before merging.
Aisha Patel: Added harness and exact run command to python/tests/perf/test_attn_microbench.py and documented workload parameters in docs/notes/attn_upgrade.md.
Miguel Santos: Concerned about regressions on rotary vs rope models. Are there fallbacks when rotary isn't supported?

Aisha Patel: Yes—runtime probes model config at load-time; if rotary/rope compatibility fails the fused kernel is skipped and we fall back to existing FlashAttentionV1 path. Added unit tests for the detection logic.
